why: Replacing the examples to teach the scorer about single high-contradiction cuts caused it to downrank those specific high-contra boundaries (producing modest average gains, especially in the ≤7 bin) but in many short-latency cases it compensated by preferring alternative splits that fragment noun phrases and enumerations, producing numerous local losses.
lesson: A later revision should avoid fixing single high-contra cuts by encouraging alternative fragmenting splits — preserve noun-phrase and enumeration integrity in short-latency (≤3–≤5) cases when de-emphasizing high-contradiction single cuts.
